titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 3
part: Spell 17, part 3 — the Eye of Ra, the lords of Maat and the seven spirits (Plates 8–10)
about: The third part of Spell 17 goes on with the commentary: the Eye of Ra in its rage is healed by Thoth, and Ra is born from Mehet-weret, the Great Flood. Ani then greets the lords of Maat and the tribunal behind Osiris and asks them to drive out his evil as they did for the seven spirits, and the glosses name the four sons of Horus, the seven spirits and the chief of the tribunal. On the papyrus it runs from Plate 8, line 70, to Plate 10, line 109, from the question on the hair raised at the time of the storm to the statement 'I am his ba in the midst of the Two Tjafi', which the next part explains.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; 'it' is the raising of the hair at the time of the storm, the statement that ends part 2. Budge's numeral 71 is printed after rf.

sentences.l: the-Eye · it-is · right · of · Ra · in · raging-its · against-him · after · sent-he · it
sentences.i: It is the right Eye of Ra in its raging against him after he had sent it out.
sentences.n: irt 'the Eye' is the eye ir with t and a stroke. imnt 'right' is the emblem of the West (R14), which also writes imn 'right', with m and t as complements and, as classifier, a cord with a loop at its end (coded V12, approximate; the sign is not clear in the print): the feminine of imny 'right', agreeing with irt (Budge: àmt). n 'of' is not made feminine. nšny·s 'its raging' is nšny, the word for the storm at the end of part 2 (its pool š a box with strokes, approximate), with the bolt ·s, 'its', the Eye's. r·f 'against him' is the mouth r and the viper ·f with its horns. m-ḫt 'after', as in part 2. hꜣb·f 'he sent' is the courtyard h, ꜣ, the foot b, two strokes and walking legs, with ·f: hꜣb 'send', a sḏm·f after m-ḫt, 'after he had sent'; the strokes are not read, and Budge's numeral 72 is printed inside the word (Budge: habi-f, 'he hath made it to depart'). sw 'it' is the dependent pronoun, the object; the Eye is feminine, but sw is written. Ra sent his Eye out against his enemies, and in its fury it turned on him.

sentences.l: (it-was) · Thoth · who-raised · the-hair · there · has-brought-he · it · (n) · living · sound · healthy · without · harm(?) · to · (its)-lord
sentences.i: It was Thoth who raised the hair from it; he has brought it, living, sound and healthy, with no harm(?) to its lord.
sentences.n: in with a noun and a participle singles out the doer: in ḏḥwty ṯs 'it was Thoth who raised'. in is the reed with a sign that is not clear in the print (coded W25, approximate; Budge: àn). ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t, two strokes and a god. ṯs is the tethering rope ṯ and the bolt s with a forked post (coded U39, approximate) and the low sign U15 as classifiers: the participle of ṯs 'raise' (Budge: θes). šn 'the hair' is the cord šn (V7) with n, two strokes and a lock of hair. im is the adverb 'there, therein', here 'from it'. in·n·f 'he has brought' is the jar on legs in (W25, approximate) with n, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·f. The bolt after it, printed after Budge's numeral 73, is split off here as the dependent pronoun s 'it', the Eye. The water n that follows has no clear place and is not translated. ꜥnḫ wḏꜣ snb 'living, sound, healthy' is written short, as after a king's name: the sign of life, the tall sign ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) for wḏꜣ and the folded cloth for snb. n bgꜣ is the arms of negation, then the foot b, the jar-stand g (approximate), ꜣ and the bird of bad things: bgꜣ is taken from its classifier as 'harm, failing', perhaps a writing of bꜣgi 'be weary, slack' with the ꜣ after g (Budge: beḳa, 'defect'); the word is doubtful. n nb 'to its lord', Ra; no suffix is written, and 'its' is supplied. Thoth, the healer, brings the Eye back whole.

sentences.l: another · saying · (wnn) · the-Eye · it-is · in · being-ill-its · in · being-its · at · weeping · for · fellow-its
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the Eye when it was ill, when it was weeping for its fellow.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. wnn is the hare wn with n twice, the verb 'be' in its doubled stem; with irt pw after it, it is taken as opening the statement and is not translated apart (Budge: unen, 'it is'). m mr·s 'in its being ill' is the hoe mr (coded U6, approximate; the print shows a stick with a small cup at its top) with m and r as complements, the bird of bad things and ·s: the infinitive of mr 'be ill' with a suffix (Budge: mer-s, 'it is sick'). m wnn·s ḥr rmi 'when it was weeping': wnn·s, with Budge's numeral 74 printed before it, and ḥr with an infinitive make the progressive, 'it was weeping'. rmi 'weep' is r and m, two reeds and the weeping eye (D9). sn·f 'its fellow' is printed as two short strokes over a small pot (coded Z4 and W24, approximate): taken as the type's form of the arrowhead sn, with the pot for its n, and ·f with its horns (Budge: sen-f). The fellow of the one eye of the sky is the other: the sun and the moon.

sentences.l: standing-up · then · by · Thoth · to · spitting · on-it
sentences.i: Then Thoth stood up to spit on it.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes psꜣgs, with a second s (Budge's 'sic'); read psg. ꜥḥꜥ is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with ꜥ and walking legs: taken as the infinitive 'standing up', with in ḏḥwty 'by Thoth' naming the doer, as in ḏd in N 'said by N' (Budge: āḥā àref àn Teḥuti, 'standeth up then Thoth'). irf 'then' is the reed, r and the viper with its horns. ḏḥwty is written here without the god. r psg 'to spit' is r with the infinitive: the stool p, the bolt s, ꜣ (not read) and the jar-stand g, then, after Budge's numeral 75, the second bolt, a curved stem with bristles and a cross-bar at its tip that cannot be identified (coded M3, approximate), and the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of what the mouth does. Budge reads pesaḳ, 'wash', and prints -nes with it as one word; here n·s, water n and the bolt, is split off as the preposition with ·s, 'on it', the Eye. The reading psg is likely but not sure. Spittle was a remedy in Egyptian healing, and Thoth is the healer of the Eye.

sentences.l: (iw) · have-seen-I · Ra · born · in · yesterday · at · the-hindquarters(?) · of · Mehet-weret
sentences.i: I have seen Ra, born yesterday from the hindquarters(?) of Mehet-weret.
sentences.n: A new statement; iw opens it. mꜣꜣ·n·i 'I have seen' is the eye with the sickle mꜣ printed beneath it, the vulture ꜣ twice, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i, here the man raising one arm. ms 'born' is the three skins ms with s and the woman giving birth (B3): the passive participle of msi. m sf 'yesterday' is the folded cloth s and the viper f with its horns, with the sun as classifier, as in part 1. r is 'at, towards'; the sense asks for 'from'. ḫpdt is the placenta ḫ, p, the hand d and t, with a fish with a hatched fin (coded K1, approximate) and two small loops (coded V1, approximate) as classifiers that cannot be identified; the reading and the sense 'hindquarters' follow Budge's χepṭet and are not sure. mḥt-wrt 'Mehet-weret', 'the Great Flood', is the crown of the north mḥ with water, the swallow wr with r and t, and a recumbent cow with an object on its back (coded E1, approximate) and a cobra as classifiers; the t of mḥt is not written (Budge: Meḥ-urt). Mehet-weret is the sky as a cow in the waters, who gives birth to the sun.

sentences.l: soundness-his · soundness-my · tie-and-turn-round
sentences.i: His soundness is my soundness, and the other way round.
sentences.n: wḏꜣ·f 'his soundness' is the chick w, the tall sign ḏꜣ (U28, approximate), ꜣ and the roll, with ·f: the noun from wḏꜣ 'be sound'. A noun set beside a noun is a sentence without a verb: 'his soundness is my soundness'. wḏꜣ·i has ·i, the man raising one arm. Budge's two groups θes and rer are joined here as ṯs-pẖr 'and vice versa', literally 'tie and turn round', the phrase that says a statement also holds the other way: a knotted cord (coded S24, approximate) for ṯs, and an oval loop (coded V10, approximate) for pẖr, whose sign, the coiled intestine, the type may draw so; Budge renders 'conversely'. 'He' is Ra, born in the line before: the dead man is well when the sun is well, and the sun when he is.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; Budge's numeral 77 is printed inside tr, before its last sign.

sentences.l: this · the-flood · of · the-sky
sentences.i: This is the flood of the sky.
sentences.n: nnw is water n, a low adze-like sign (coded U19, approximate, the adze nw), the pot nw and the chick w: taken as the demonstrative nn 'this, these' in a later spelling, standing first in a sentence without a verb, 'this is …' (Budge: ennu, 'This is'); the same group means 'those' in lines 80 and 86. The construction is not sure. nwy 'the flood, the waters' is written with the same signs, a second n, two reeds y and, as classifiers, the three water lines, a canal (coded N36, approximate), two small spool-shaped signs (coded N23, approximate) and a stroke (Budge: ennui, 'the water'). n pt 'of the sky'. The flood of the sky is the Great Flood, Mehet-weret, of line 76.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-image · it-is · of · the-Eye · of-Ra · in-the-morning · at · birth-his · day · every
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the image of the Eye of Ra in the morning, at his birth every day.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. twt 'image' is t, w and t with a standing mummy-shaped figure (A53) and the roll as classifiers; Budge's numeral 78 is printed inside it. n 'of'. rꜥ is the god with the sun on his head alone. dwꜣw 'in the morning' is the star dwꜣ with ꜣ and w and the sun; the t and w after the sun are not read (Budge: ṭuau-tu). They could make dwꜣ·tw 'one adores', but the sun classifier asks for 'morning', and the reading is not sure. r mswt·f 'at his birth': the skins with s, w, the woman giving birth, t and a second w, which is not read, and ·f. rꜥ nb 'every day' is the sun with its stroke and nb, as in part 2 (Budge: hru neb). Every dawn the sun is born again from the sky.

sentences.l: as-for · Mehet-weret · the-Sound-Eye · it-is · of · Ra
sentences.i: As for Mehet-weret, it is the Sound Eye of Ra.
sentences.n: ir 'as for' sets the name first as the topic, as in part 2; Budge's numeral 79 is printed after it. mḥt-wrt as in line 76, with the cow (approximate) and the cobra. wḏꜣt 'the Sound Eye' is the chick w, the tall sign ḏꜣ (U28, approximate), ꜣ and t, with the eye with the falcon's markings (D10), as in part 2. The great cow of the sky is the Eye of the sun itself.

sentences.l: because · as-for · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · one · great · among · those · gods · who-are-in · the-following · of-Horus
sentences.i: For the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, is a great one among those gods who are in the following of Horus.
sentences.n: ḥr-ntt 'because' is the face ḥr with its stroke, n and t, with two strokes; the second t is not written, and Budge's footnote number is printed beside the group (Budge: ḥerenti, 'Therefore'). It ties this statement to the gloss before it, and 'for' renders it. ir 'as for' puts the Osiris Ani first. wsir is the low seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye; Ani ends with the man on a chair (A51). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written short, the plinth and the oar, with no sickle. wꜥ wr 'a great one' is the harpoon wꜥ with a stroke and the arm, then the swallow wr with r: a noun with its adjective, the predicate. m nnw nṯrw 'among those gods': nnw as in line 77, nṯrw three flags. imyw ḫt ḥr 'who are in the following of Horus': imyw with a god and a stroke (Budge's numeral 81 is printed before them), then the branch ḫt with ḫ, t and walking legs, and the falcon with a god. The dead man takes his place in the company of the gods around Horus.

sentences.l: is-said · upon · head-his · beloved · lord-his
sentences.i: This is said on behalf of(?) him, the beloved of his lord.
sentences.n: ḏdw 'is said' is a tall tapering sign standing for ḏ (U28, approximate, as in part 1), the hand d and the chick w, with the man with hand to mouth and a stroke: the passive sḏm of ḏd, with the w it sometimes has (Budge: t'eṭu, 'Spoken'). ḥr tp·f is literally 'upon his head': the face ḥr and the head tp, each with its stroke, and ·f. Its sense here, 'on his behalf, concerning him', follows Budge ('for him') and is not sure. mry is the hoe mr with r, two reeds y, the chick w and the man with hand to mouth: the passive participle of mri 'love', 'beloved', with nb·f 'his lord' (the basket, a god and ·f) after it as a direct genitive; the w is not read. ḏdw could instead be the plural participle 'who say', going with the gods of line 80 ('who speak on his behalf'); the unit is read here as a passive statement, and neither reading is sure. 'Beloved of his lord' is an old epithet of a faithful servant, said here of the dead man.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; Budge's line 82 begins after pw.

sentences.l: Imsety · Hapy · Duamutef · Qebehsenuf
sentences.i: They are Imsety, Hapy, Duamutef and Qebehsenuf.
sentences.n: The gloss gives four names and no pw; 'they are' is supplied. They are the four sons of Horus, the gods who guard the dead man's inner organs, and the 'gods in the following of Horus' of line 80. msṯi 'Imsety' is the sign Aa15 for m, the bolt s, the tethering rope ṯ and the reed, with a god: the name is written without its first i and with ṯ (Budge: Mesθà). ḥpy 'Hapy' is two stacked chevrons in the print (coded Aa5, approximate), taken as the sign ḥp, with p as complement, two reeds and a god (Budge: Ḥāpi). dwꜣ-mwt-f 'Duamutef', 'He who adores his mother', is the star dwꜣ, the large vulture mwt with t, and f, the viper with its horns, with a god (Budge: Ṭuamāutef). qbḥ-snw-f 'Qebehsenuf', 'He who refreshes his brothers', is a tall jar with a crossed top (coded W14, approximate) for qbḥ, a tall shaft with a crossed foot (coded T22, approximate) for sn, plural strokes for the plural snw, and f with a god (Budge: Qebḥsennuf).

sentences.l: hail · to-you · lords · of-Maat · the-tribunal · behind · Osiris · who-give · slaughter · among · the-wrong(doers) · who-are-in-the-following · of-Hetep-sekhus
sentences.i: Hail to you, lords of Maat, tribunal behind Osiris, who deal out slaughter among the wrongdoers(?), who are in the following of Hetep-sekhus!
sentences.n: A new speech, to the gods of the tribunal. ind ḥr·tn 'hail to you' is the reed and a staff (coded Aa27, approximate) for nḏ, with the cobra ḏ and a roll, then the face ḥr with its stroke and ·tn, as in Spell 1. nbw mꜣꜥt 'lords of Maat': the basket with w and a stroke, then the sickle mꜣ crossing the plinth mꜣꜥ, t, the arm, the feather, the roll and a stroke. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'tribunal' is ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) twice with the pot and t between, a barred sign (coded N1, approximate), a god and a stroke, as in Spell 1. ḥꜣ 'behind' with the back of a head, as in part 2. ddyw 'who give' is the giving arm twice, two reeds, w and a stroke: the plural of the imperfective participle of rdi, with its doubled stem dd. šꜥd 'slaughter' is the pool (approximate) with ꜥ and d, a knife and a spiky cone (coded M44, approximate) and plural strokes, as in part 2. isft 'wrong' is the reed, a reed bundle (M40) for is, s, the viper f, ꜣ (not read), t and the bird of bad things with plural strokes (Budge: àsfat, 'defects'); 'the wrongdoers' is taken from the plural, and is not sure. ḥtp-sḫws 'Hetep-sekhus' is the offering mat with t and p, then s and ḫ with a bent arm (coded D41, approximate), w and s with a cobra; Budge's numeral 85 is printed inside it.

sentences.l: behold-you · me · have-come-I · to-you
sentences.i: See, I have come to you.
sentences.n: Budge's group mā-ten-uà is split here into two words. m·tn 'behold' is the owl m and the arm ꜥ, which is not read, as in mk in the introduction to Spell 125 (the print gives the arm as a flat sign with a tab), with ·tn: the particle mk with the plural 'you' in place of its k, addressed to the gods (Budge: 'grant ye'). wi 'me' is the chick w and the man raising one arm: the dependent pronoun, the subject after m·tn. ii·kwi 'I have come' is the reeds with legs ii, i and walking legs, with the stative ending ·kwi (the basket, the chick and the seated man). ḫr·tn 'to you' is the placenta ḫ and r with ·tn. m·tn wi with the stative presents the speaker: 'see, here I am, come to you'.

sentences.l: may-drive-out-you · evil · all · that-is-mine · like · that · which-did-you · for · spirits · seven · these · who-are-in · the-following · of · lord-their · Sepa
sentences.i: May you drive out all the evil that is mine, as you did for these seven spirits who are in the following of their lord Sepa.
sentences.n: dr·tn 'may you drive out' is the hand d, r and the low sign U15, with ·tn: a sḏm·f with ·tn as a wish (Budge: ṭer-ten, 'Destroy ye'). ḏwt 'evil' is the mountain ḏw (outlined in the print) with t, w, the bird of bad things and plural strokes; Budge's numeral 86 is printed inside it. nb 'all' is not made feminine. iry·i 'that is mine' is iry with a seated figure holding a staff (coded A47, approximate), the roll and a stroke, and ·i. mi nnw ir·n·tn 'like what you did': the jug mi with i, nnw 'that' as in line 77, and ir·n·tn, the eye ir with the n of the relative form and ·tn. ꜣḫw 'spirits' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, w and a seated figure holding a flail (coded A52, approximate) with a stroke. The seven is printed as three strokes over four (coded Z15f): sfḫ 'seven', the number after its noun. ipw 'these' (Budge's numeral 87 inside it). imyw šmsw 'who are in the following': šmsw is the follower's staff (T18) with s and walking legs, 'following, retinue'. nb·sn 'their lord' has a god. spꜣ 'Sepa' is the bolt s, the flying bird pꜣ with ꜣ, a centipede (no code exists; coded I14) and a god (Budge: Sepa).

sentences.l: made · Anubis · places-their · on-day · that · of · come · then · there
sentences.i: Anubis made their places on that day of 'Come, then, there!'
sentences.n: Budge's two groups àri and en are joined here as ir·n, the eye ir with the n of the sḏm·n·f: 'Anubis made'. inpw 'Anubis' is the reed, n, p and w with a god. st·sn 'their places' is the seat st with t and the house sign, with ·sn; n and the plural strokes of ·sn stand in Budge's square brackets and are restored. hrw pwy 'on that day', as in part 2. mi 'come!' is the owl m, the arm (a flat sign with a tab in the print), i, two strokes and walking legs: the imperative of the verbs of coming, written as in the address after Spell 125. ir·k 'then, you' is the reed, r and ·k: r with a suffix after an imperative. im 'there' is the reed and the owl. 'Come, then, there!' names the day by its call: the day the dead are summoned to the places made for them.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; Budge's line 89 begins at rf.

sentences.l: as-for · these · lords · of-Maat · Thoth · it-is · and · Isdes · lord · of-the-West
sentences.i: As for these lords of Maat, it is Thoth and Isdes, lord of the West.
sentences.n: nn 'these' is two sedges and two waters, as in part 2, here with no n between it and its noun. nbw mꜣꜥt as in line 83, but the plinth is not printed: the sickle mꜣ over a flat sign with a tab (coded D36), t, the feather, the roll and a stroke. ḏḥwty pw 'it is Thoth': the ibis on its standard with t and two strokes. ḥnꜥ 'and'. isds 'Isdes' is the reed, the folded cloth s, the hand d and the bolt s, with a small jar (coded W22, approximate) and a god (Budge: Àsṭes); Budge's numeral 90 is printed inside it. nb imntt 'lord of the West': the emblem of the West with t twice and the desert hills. Isdes is a god of the judgement of the dead, often named beside Thoth.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · behind · Osiris · Imsety · Hapy · Duamutef · Qebehsenuf · those · it-is · who-are · behind · the · Foreleg · in · the-sky · northern
sentences.i: As for the tribunal behind Osiris, Imsety, Hapy, Duamutef and Qebehsenuf, they are those who are behind the Foreleg in the northern sky.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ḥꜣ in red. ḏꜣḏꜣt as in line 83, its pot with lugs (approximate). wsir has the eye before the tall seat and a god. The four sons of Horus are named as in line 82: Imsety begins with a long flat sign (coded Aa15, approximate); Duamutef has ꜣ, a man with raised arms (coded A28, approximate) and the roll as classifiers, its t not written; Qebehsenuf has a jar on a stand (coded W16, approximate) for qbḥ, the shaft sn with n, the pot and w, and plural strokes. nꜣ pw 'they are those': nꜣ, water n and ꜣ, the demonstrative of later Egyptian, with pw. nty m-sꜣ 'who are behind': m-sꜣ is the owl and a sign like a reed shelter (Aa18) for sꜣ, 'back', with a stroke, the compound preposition; Budge's numeral 92 is printed inside it. pꜣ ḫpš 'the Foreleg': the article pꜣ (the flying bird and ꜣ), then ḫ, p and š with the foreleg of an ox (F23), a star and a god as classifiers: the constellation of the Great Bear. pt mḥtt 'the northern sky': mḥ with a canal sign (approximate) and t twice. The four sons stand among the northern stars, which never set.

sentences.l: as-for · who-give · slaughter · among · the-wrong(doers) · who-are-in-the-following · of-Hetep-sekhus · Sobek · it-is · who-is-in · the-water
sentences.i: As for those who deal out slaughter among the wrongdoers(?), who are in the following of Hetep-sekhus, it is Sobek, who is in the water.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir ddyw šꜥd m isft in red. ddyw and šꜥd are written as in line 83, the spiky cone of šꜥd approximate; Budge's numeral 93 is printed inside šꜥd. isft here has the reed and a tall roll with a tie (coded Y1a, approximate) where line 84 has the reed bundle is; it is taken as the same sign. imyw-ḫt is one word in the print, as in line 84. ḥtp-sḫws has two strokes after the bent arm (D41, approximate), which are not read. sbk 'Sobek' is the folded cloth s, the foot b and the basket k with a crocodile on a shrine (coded I4, approximate) and a god (Budge: Sebek). imy mw 'who is in the water': imy, the crossed planks with the owl and two strokes, and the three water lines for mw (Budge: māa, 'waters'). Sobek, the crocodile, is the god of the waters.

sentences.l: as-for · Hetep-sekhus · the-Eye · it-is · of · Ra
sentences.i: As for Hetep-sekhus, it is the Eye of Ra.
sentences.n: ḥtp-sḫws as in line 93, with two strokes after the bent arm. irt 'the Eye' with t and a stroke. nt 'of' is feminine here, agreeing with irt; Budge's numeral 95 is printed after it. The fierce goddess whom the punishers follow is the Eye of the sun, as at the beginning of this part.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-flame · is-it · following · Osiris · at · burning · the-bas · of · enemies-his
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the flame; it is in the following of Osiris, burning the bas of his enemies.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd nsrt wnn·s m-ḫt in red. nsrt 'the flame' is water n, a tall stick hooked at the top that cannot be identified (coded T14, approximate) and is not read, the bolt s, r and t, with a tall flame-like sign (coded Q7, approximate) as classifier (Budge: nesert). wnn·s 'it is' is wnn with ·s, the flame. m-ḫt 'following, behind' as in line 71. wsir with the low seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye. ḥr sꜣmt 'burning' is ḥr with the infinitive of sꜣm 'burn': the bolt s, the pintail duck sꜣ (G39) with ꜣ, the owl m and t, with the flame (approximate) as classifier (Budge: samt); Budge's numeral 96 is printed inside it. bꜣw 'the bas' is the jabiru with the bowl and flame at its foot, a stroke, a god and a stroke. nw 'of' is the plural genitive, the pot with a stroke. ḫftyw·f 'his enemies' is written with the vulture ꜣ, which is not read, as in part 1, and a kneeling man (coded A14, approximate). The flame is the fire of the uraeus, turned on the enemies of Osiris.

sentences.l: as-for · (now) · evil · all · belonging-to · the-Osiris · the-scribe · of-the-god's-offerings · of · the-gods · all · Ani · true-of-voice · since · came-down-he · from · the-womb · of · mother-his
sentences.i: As for all the evil that belongs to the Osiris, the scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods, Ani, true of voice, since he came down from the womb of his mother —
sentences.n: ir ẖrt as in part 2, ẖrt taken as the particle grt. ḏwt nb iry 'all the evil that belongs to' as in line 85, iry with the seated figure (A47, approximate). wsir has the low seat (Q2, approximate) before the eye. sš ḥtp-nṯr n nṯrw nbw 'the scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods': the offering mat with t and p and the flag nṯr; nbw is the basket with plural strokes. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written short, with no sickle. ḏr 'since' is the bundle ḏr (M36) with r, as a conjunction before a verb form. hꜣy·f 'he came down' is the courtyard h, ꜣ, two reeds and walking legs with ·f: a sḏm·f of hꜣi; Budge's numeral 98 is printed inside it. m ẖt n mwt·f 'from the womb of his mother': ẖt is the belly with t and a stroke; mwt·f is the vulture with t and ·f, then a seated figure like a god's (it may be the woman, B1) and a seated man as classifiers after the suffix. Budge brackets the f in his transliteration and adds '(sic)', though the viper is printed: nothing is changed here. No predicate follows the ir phrase. It may itself be the gloss on 'all the evil that is mine' of line 85, the evil of a whole life since birth; or a clause is missing. The translation gives what is written.

sentences.l: as-for · (now) · the-spirits · these · seven · Imsety · Hapy · Duamutef · Qebehsenuf · Maa-itef-ef · Khery-baqef · Horus-Khenty-irty
sentences.i: As for these seven spirits, they are Imsety, Hapy, Duamutef, Qebehsenuf, Maa-itef-ef, Khery-baqef and Horus-Khenty-irty.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes dwꜣ-mwt-r, with the mouth r where the viper f should be; read dwꜣ-mwt-f. The papyrus writes ir ẖrt ꜣḫw ipw 7 in red, with the numeral after ipw here (in lines 86 and 102 it comes before it); ipw has a single stroke, and Budge's numeral 99 is printed inside it. 'They are' is supplied. The four sons of Horus are written as in line 90; Imsety begins with a thin trapezoid (coded Aa11, approximate), taken as the sign Aa15 for m, and Qebehsenuf has a god before its f. mꜣꜣ-itf-f 'He who sees his father' is mꜣꜣ (the sickle, the eye, ꜣ twice), itf with the viper and a god, and f (Budge: Maa-atef-f). ẖry-bꜣq-f 'He who is under his moringa tree' is the sign ẖr with r and two strokes y, a flat roll that is not read, b and q with a tree (M1) for bꜣq, its ꜣ not written, and f with a god (Budge: Kheri-beq-f). ḥr-ḫnty-irty 'Horus Foremost of the Two Eyes' is the falcon with a god, ḫnty (the jar-stand ḫnt with n, t and two strokes), and the eye written twice (Budge: Ḥeru-khenti-maa, reading the eyes as mꜣꜣ 'see'). The seven are the four sons of Horus and three more gods.

sentences.l: placing-them · by · Anubis · as · protection · of-the-burial · of · Osiris
sentences.i: Anubis set them as protection over the burial of Osiris.
sentences.n: rdit·sn is the mouth r and the plain arm (D36), standing for the giving arm as in part 1, with t and ·sn: the infinitive rdit 'placing', with ·sn 'them' as its object, and in inpw 'by Anubis' naming the doer (Budge: erṭāt-sen àn Ànpu, 'placed then Anubis'). inpw here has the jackal-headed god (C6). m sꜣ 'as protection' is the shelter sꜣ (V17) with a stroke and plural strokes (Budge: sau, 'protectors'). qrs 'the burial' is the bolt over q and r with a lying mummy (coded A54, approximate) and the low sign U15, as in part 1; nt 'of' agrees with qrst, whose t is not written. wsir has the eye before the tall seat. Anubis, god of embalming, set the seven as guards around the body of Osiris.

sentences.l: another · saying · behind · the-place-of-purification · of · Osiris
sentences.i: Another saying: they are behind the place of purification of Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd m-sꜣ in red. Budge's groups em and sa, split by his numeral 102, are joined here as m-sꜣ 'behind', as in line 91. wꜥbt 'the place of purification' is the vase pouring water over a leg (D60), the sign wꜥb, with t, water and the house sign: wꜥbt, 'the pure place', where the body was washed and embalmed (Budge: àbt, 'the place of purification'). nt 'of' agrees with it. No subject is written; 'they are' is supplied. wsir has the eye before the tall seat and a god. The guardians stand behind the embalming place of Osiris.

sentences.l: another · saying · as-for · the-spirits · seven · these · Nedjeh-nedjeh · Iaqed-qed · In-redi-nef-besef-khenty-hehef · Aq-her-imy-unutef
sentences.i: Another saying: as for these seven spirits, they are Nedjeh-nedjeh, Iaqed-qed, In-redi-nef-besef-khenty-hehef, Aq-her-imy-unutef,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd ir ꜣḫw 7 ipw in red; ipw has the coil w, and Budge's numeral 103 follows it. The seven names run on into the next unit; they are left as names, their sense not clear. nḏḥ-nḏḥ is water n, a cobra-like sign for ḏ (I10, approximate) and the wick ḥ, written twice, with a god (Budge: Net'eḥ-net'eḥ). iꜣqd-qd is the reed and ꜣ, then a tall wedge (coded Aa28, approximate) for qd with d and a pot, which is not read, written twice, with a god (Budge: Àaqeṭqeṭ). The third name begins with a sign that cannot be identified (coded V26, approximate; Budge: àn), then rdi (r and the giving arm), n·f, b with a flame (coded Q7, approximate) for bs 'flame' and f, ḫnty 'foremost', the shelter h twice with the flame for hh 'heat'(?) and f with a god: perhaps 'who … his flame, foremost of his heat'; Budge's numeral 104 is printed before its last viper. ꜥq-ḥr-imy-wnwt-f is a long-necked bird (coded G35, approximate) for ꜥq 'enter' with q and walking legs, ḥr 'face', imy 'who is in' and wnwt 'hour' with the star and the sun, and f with a god (Budge: Aq-ḥer-àmmi-unnut-f). All these readings are doubtful.

sentences.l: Desher-irty-imy-hut-ines · Webes-her-per-em-khetkhet · Maa-em-gereh-in-nef-em-heru
sentences.i: Desher-irty-imy-hut-ines, Webes-her-per-em-khetkhet and Maa-em-gereh-in-nef-em-heru.
sentences.n: dšr-irty-imy-ḥwt-ins is the hand d, the pool š (approximate) and r with a long-necked bird (coded G27, approximate), the eye twice and a god, then imy, the mansion ḥwt with t and the house sign, and ins, the reed, the fish in (K1), n and s with a fringed cloth (coded S28, approximate) and a stroke: perhaps 'Red of eyes, who is in the house of red linen' (Budge: Ṭesher-maa-àmmi-ḥet-Ànes, reading the eyes as maa); Budge's numeral 105 is printed inside it. wbs-ḥr-pr-m-ḫtḫt, the first word under Budge's heading for Plate 10, is w, b and s with a flame (approximate) and a god, ḥr 'face', pr 'who comes forth' (the house, r and walking legs), and m ḫtḫt, the branch ḫt with t and ḫ written twice, with walking legs: perhaps '… of face, who comes forth backwards'; wbs is not identified (Budge: Ubes-ḥrà-per-em-khetkhet). mꜣꜣ-m-grḥ-in-n-f-m-hrw is mꜣꜣ 'see' (the sickle, the eye and ꜣ twice), m grḥ 'by night' (the jar-stand g, approximate, r and ḥ with the night sky N2, approximate), a stick with a loop at its top (coded S34, approximate), taken as in 'bring', with n and n·f, and m hrw 'by day': 'He who sees by night and brings by day' (Budge: Maa-em-ḳerḥ-àn-nef-em-hru). These readings too are doubtful.

sentences.l: as-for · the-chief · of-the-tribunal · of · those · of · […]-his · Horus · who-protects · father-his
sentences.i: As for the chief of the tribunal of those of his […], he is Horus, who protects his father.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir ḥry-tp ḏꜣḏꜣt n nꜣ n irwd·f in red. ḥry-tp 'chief' is the face ḥr with r and two strokes y, then the head tp with its stroke, as in Spell 22; Budge prints the head but reads only ḥeri. ḏꜣḏꜣt as in line 83, its signs in another order (U28 approximate); Budge's numeral 107 is printed inside it. n nꜣ n 'of those of': water n, then nꜣ (n and ꜣ), then n. The next word is the reed, r and a knotted cord (coded T12, approximate; rd or rwd) with the house sign, and ·f; Budge reads àruṭ-f, 'his hall'. No such word can be confirmed, and it is shown as […]. ḥr 'Horus' follows without pw; 'he is' is supplied. nḏ-ḥr 'who protects' joins Budge's net' and ḥrà, as in part 2: the staff nḏ (Aa27) with the pot for n and the low sign U15, then the face with its stroke. itf·f 'his father' with the viper, a god and ·f. Horus, the son who stood up for his father, presides over the tribunal.

sentences.l: as-for · (now) · day · that · come · then · there · the-saying · of-Osiris · it-is · to · Ra · come · then · there
sentences.i: As for that day of 'Come, then, there!', it is the saying of Osiris to Ra: 'Come, then, there!'
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir ẖrt hrw pf mi ir·k im in red. pf 'that' is the stool p and the viper f: the masculine demonstrative, after its noun. No n is written before mi here. mi 'come!' is the owl lying over the arm, i, two strokes and walking legs, as in line 88. ḏd wsir pw n rꜥ: ḏd, the cobra over the hand, is the infinitive 'saying', with wsir after it as a direct genitive, 'the saying of Osiris', and n rꜥ 'to Ra', the god alone. Budge renders 'the saying to Osiris by Ra'; but n does not name a doer, and the grammar makes Osiris the speaker. Budge's numeral 109 is printed inside the second ir·k. The god of the dead calls the sun to the meeting of the two in the world below.

sentences.l: is-seen(?) · is-assigned(?) · seat-my · to · the-West
sentences.i: It is seen(?) that my seat is assigned(?) in the West.
sentences.n: This line is doubtful. mꜣꜣ·tw is the sickle mꜣ with the eye, ꜣ twice, t and w: mꜣꜣ 'see' with the passive tw, 'one sees, it is seen' (Budge: maa-tu, 'see'). The next group, which Budge leaves without transliteration, is the horned viper with its × crossed by a stick ending in a hanging loop (coded V25, approximate). It is taken, doubtfully, as the sign wḏ 'command, assign', with the viper not read: wḏ is often written with the cobra ḏ as its complement, and the snake joined to the stick may be that cobra drawn as the viper. wḏ is taken as a passive sḏm, 'is assigned', with st·i as its subject; Budge's English 'decreed is it' may rest on the same guess. st·i 'my seat' joins Budge's set and à: the bolt and t, writing st 'seat', with ·i, the man raising one arm. st 'seat' usually has the seat sign; bolt and t alone is the usual spelling of the dependent pronoun st 'it', and Budge reads it so, with the man as 'for me' ('decreed is it for me'). r imntt 'to the West', the emblem of the West with t twice and the desert hills. wḏ r 'assign to' is the verb used in part 1 of Osiris assigned to Set-Imentet.

sentences.l: I · ba-his · who-is-in-the-midst-of · the-Two-Tjafi(?)
sentences.i: I am his ba, who is in the midst of the Two Tjafi(?).
sentences.n: A new statement. ink 'I' is the pot in and the basket k, without a seated figure. bꜣ·f 'his ba' is the jabiru bꜣ with the bowl and flame at its foot, a stroke printed high and a god, and ·f. ḥry-ib 'who is in the midst of' is the face ḥr and the heart ib, each with its stroke, as in the hymn to Osiris. ṯꜣfy is a small bird with a raised wing (coded G47, approximate), the sign ṯꜣ, the viper f and two strokes y, the dual ending, with two gods; before the bird the print has a small × (coded Z9), which is not read. Budge reads T'afi, 'the two Tchafi'; the pair is not named elsewhere in the papyrus so far, and the reading is not sure. 'His' points back to a god not named in the statement; the next part opens with the question on it.
